title: Normalized Security Finding
description: The canonical finding shape used by security-automation/finding_triage.py. Every input format (Checkov, Bandit, the project's IAM policy checker, AWS Security Hub ASFF, or hand-written JSON) is transformed into this shape before any scoring, deduplication or reporting happens. Keeping one internal shape is what makes risk comparable across tools: a 'HIGH' from Bandit and a 'HIGH' from Checkov mean different things until they are both mapped onto the same scale.

finding_id.description: Stable identifier. Derived deterministically from (source, category, resource, title) when absent, so the same defect keeps the same id across runs and can be referenced in a ticket.

source.description: Tool or process that produced the finding, e.g. 'checkov', 'bandit', 'iam-policy-checker', 'securityhub', 'manual-review'.

resource.description: What the finding is about: a Terraform address, a file path with line, an AWS ARN, or an application component.

category.description: Risk domain. Drives both the category weight in scoring and the default owner assignment.

severity.description: Normalized severity. Tool-specific labels (ERROR, WARNING, 7.5, INFORMATIONAL) are mapped onto this scale during normalization.

description.description: Longer explanation. Must not contain credentials, customer data, or raw log content.

status.description: Workflow state. 'accepted_risk' and 'false_positive' are terminal and are excluded from the open-risk statistics, but are still reported so an accepted risk cannot be quietly forgotten.

first_observed.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of first observation. Preserved across runs via --previous so finding age is real rather than reset on every scan.

last_observed.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent observation.

remediation.description: What to actually do about it.

owner.description: Assigned team or role. Normally derived from the configurable assignment rules; an explicit value here overrides them.

references.description: CWE identifiers, OWASP categories, vendor documentation.
